solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Idly, I cut off ability to think clearly (8)

indicatorNotes.off: something that has gone off is spoiled, so the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: Someone drifting idly through the day confesses to having shut down their own clear thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Idly' makes it look like an adverb describing how things were cut; it is simply four letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clearness of mind and expression is exactly what the word names.

entries.clue: Less serious match? (7)

blocks.note: the comparative of light in its sense of not heavy in mood
not a game but something you strike; the question mark says the answer only does a match's job

annotation.surface: A sports fan hopes the next fixture will be a less intense, friendlier game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting fixture, but it is the kind you strike to make a flame, and a LIGHTER does the same job.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: light-hearted in the comparative, and the pocket gadget that stands in for a match.

entries.clue: Nobleman is important briefly (5)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: 'is important' = matters, as in 'every vote matters'; take the synonym ending in S and cut that S off

annotation.surface: A remark that a titled aristocrat matters, said in passing.
annotation.walkthrough: Dropping the S from COUNTS leaves the European title.
annotation.definitionFit: A European title of nobility, roughly equal in rank to a British earl.

entries.clue: Passed round whisky for one feeling down (10)

indicatorNotes.round: the first word goes round the other piece, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.for one: whisky is just one example of the broader category

blocks.note: whisky is one kind of spirit

annotation.surface: Someone passes a glass of whisky round to cheer up a friend who is feeling low.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passed round' looks like handing drinks about; 'passed' is really the euphemism for dying, and 'round' is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having lost heart and spirits is feeling down.

entries.clue: Acrobat scratching bottom in awkward fall (6)

indicatorNotes.scratching bottom: scratching out the bottom letter, as this is a down clue

blocks.note: an acrobat who does somersaults, a seven-letter word ending in R; that bottom letter is scratched out

annotation.surface: A circus acrobat scratches an itchy behind mid-air and comes down badly.
annotation.walkthrough: The acrobat is a TUMBLER. 'Scratching bottom' is comic surface, but in a down clue the bottom of the word is its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word suggests a fall that is sudden and ungainly rather than controlled.

entries.clue: Assist Elizabeth to some extent (4)

indicatorNotes.to some extent: only part of the next word is used

annotation.surface: A modest request to help someone called Elizabeth a little.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside a single word, which makes it easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though the word usually implies helping with wrongdoing, as in 'aid and abet'.

entries.clue: Reporter’s revealing attitude (7)

indicatorNotes.Reporter’s: a reporter speaks the word, so we hear a sound-alike

blocks.note: revealing = baring, as in baring your teeth

annotation.surface: A journalist's exposé that shows what someone really thinks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revealing attitude' reads as a single phrase, but the definition is just the last word, and BARING and BEARING are said the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the way someone carries themselves shows their manner or attitude.

entries.clue: Come into contact with tip of trident? That hurt! (5)

indicatorNotes.tip of: the tip of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: what you cry when something hurts

annotation.surface: Someone brushes against the point of a trident and yelps.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation is not commentary: 'That hurt!' is the ordinary cry OUCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: making physical contact.

entries.clue: Horrible to leave me filled with regrets (8)

indicatorNotes.filled with: GO + ME has another word put inside it

annotation.surface: Someone finds it horrible to be abandoned and left full of remorse.
annotation.walkthrough: RUES goes in after the G of GOME, not between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something so unpleasant it causes horror or disgust.

entries.clue: Banned university club making a comeback (4)

indicatorNotes.making a comeback: coming back means running the letters the other way

blocks.note: a cricket or baseball bat is a club

annotation.surface: A university society that had been banned is being revived.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society to go with 'university', but it is the thing you hit a ball with. TABU is a variant spelling of taboo.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a taboo thing is forbidden by custom, so banned.

entries.clue: Not working and disorganised: unacceptable (3,2,5)

blocks.note: the sign hung on a broken machine
British informal: behaviour that crosses a line

annotation.surface: A complaint about a broken, chaotic office, summed up as simply not good enough.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of the one phrase. In British speech, calling behaviour 'out of order' means it is unacceptable.
annotation.definitionFit: All three senses are idioms of the one phrase: broken, jumbled, and in British usage improper.

entries.clue: Show disapproval: it set back everyone playing (5)

indicatorNotes.set back: a thing set back is moved backwards, so IT is written from its end to its start

blocks.note: tut is the click of disapproval

annotation.surface: Someone tuts at a performance where everybody played at once and it went badly.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon suggests 'Show disapproval' is being defined by what follows; it is wordplay, and the definition is at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction telling all performers to play together.

entries.clue: Uncouth learner is hard to keep out (7)

indicatorNotes.to keep: L + IS + H holds OUT inside it

annotation.surface: A boorish student is difficult to keep out of somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To keep out' looks like a single phrase meaning exclude; here L-IS-H keeps the word OUT inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: behaving like a lout, rough and ill-mannered.

entries.clue: Put right tune on Queen record (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, the tune comes on after the other pieces

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: Someone fixes a song on a record by the band Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen record' suggests the rock band, but each word is its own abbreviation, and the tune goes last because it is 'on' them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to mend something broken.

entries.clue: Quietly putting down orchestra’s performance? (7)

blocks.note: p = piano, the musical marking for quietly

annotation.surface: An orchestra sets its instruments down softly after a concert.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as by example: what an orchestra performs with is its instruments, and the performance itself is the music-making.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the music an orchestra makes is one instance of the word.

entries.clue: Neglect to illegally copy contract in the end (6)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only the final letter of contract is used

blocks.note: to forge is to make an illegal copy

annotation.surface: Someone decides not to bother forging a contract after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Neglect to' reads as the start of a sentence about failing to do something; 'to' is only the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to fail to attend to something, as in 'forget your duties'.

entries.clue: Trampled rodent running round bottom of bed (7)

indicatorNotes.running: running water is moving, so the letters move
indicatorNotes.round: the rearranged letters go round the D
indicatorNotes.bottom of: in a down clue, the bottom of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A trampled mouse had been scurrying around the foot of a bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rodent' pretends to be the poor creature that got trampled, but it is just the fodder, and it very nearly spells the answer already.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: past participle of tread, walked on heavily.

entries.clue: Type of power harnessing river current (6)

indicatorNotes.harnessing: STEAM holds R in harness, inside it

annotation.surface: A hydroelectric scheme harnesses a river's current to make power.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all about hydro power, so 'river current' looks like one idea; the river is only R, and current alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a steady flow of water, as in the Gulf Stream.

entries.clue: Idle act mangled speech (7)

indicatorNotes.mangled: the letters are crushed out of shape

annotation.surface: A careless performance garbled a speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mangled speech' looks like one phrase for garbled words, but 'mangled' works on the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Speech in its sense of a way of talking; a regional variety of a language.

entries.clue: Compulsion to remove uniform clothing (5)

indicatorNotes.to remove: to remove something is to take it away, so one letter comes out of the word

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet; removed from DURESS

annotation.surface: Someone is forced to take off a uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform clothing' looks like one phrase, but uniform is the U taken out and clothing alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for garments collectively, as in 'formal dress'.

entries.clue: Unfashionable party cap (5)

annotation.surface: A party hat that has gone out of style.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like headgear to wear at the party, but it is a verb: to cap a story is to top it.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense of cap: to better or top what someone else has done.

entries.clue: Implements terms officials offered loan sharks originally (5)

indicatorNotes.originally: each word gives its original, first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Terms Officials Offered Loan Sharks

annotation.surface: Regulators set the terms under which loan sharks may operate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Implements' reads as a verb, officials putting terms into effect, but it is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the plural noun: instruments used to do a job.

entries.clue: Wickedness, as it happens, is returning (4)

indicatorNotes.returning: the word comes back the other way

blocks.note: a broadcast shown as it happens is live

annotation.surface: A remark that wickedness, by chance, is making a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' reads as a throwaway 'by chance'; it means in real time.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as a noun: moral badness in general.

entries.clue: Complaint by senior teacher lacking in empathy (4,4)

blocks.note: the head is the head teacher, the principal
a cold person shows no warmth or empathy

annotation.surface: A grievance lodged by a headteacher who is short on sympathy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance, but here it is an ailment. In Britain the head is the headteacher.
annotation.definitionFit: Complaint in its medical sense, a minor illness; this one blocks the nose and sinuses.

entries.clue: Herb dip to go with last of meze (4)

indicatorNotes.last of: only the final letter of meze is used

annotation.surface: A herby dip served alongside the final dish of a meze spread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dip' pretends to be a sauce like hummus; it is the verb, to sag. Meze is a spread of small Mediterranean dishes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the grey-leaved kitchen herb used in stuffing is one member of it.

entries.clue: Lock up mischievous child with wrong irons (8)

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters are set out wrongly

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child

annotation.surface: A naughty child is put in chains.
annotation.walkthrough: Irons are also shackles, which fits the surface of locking someone up, but here the word is only anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put someone in prison or confine them.
